## Natural history notes

A small round lady beetle characterized by its glossy red to orange wing covers, black head with pale markings, and lack of spots on the back. In Florida, it is common in gardens, fields, citrus groves, forest edges, parks, yards, and other habitats where aphids and other soft-bodied insects are present. Both adults and larvae are predators, feeding mainly on aphids, scale insects, whiteflies, and other small plant-feeding insects, making this species an important natural enemy in gardens and agricultural systems.
